name: Canonical Schema Mapper
description: Maps the many names a field goes by (aliases) to one canonical name, combines fields that hold the same thing, and converts each to a set type with an optional default, following rules kept as data (typed into the block or in a CSV file), working through the data in chunks so large inputs never have to fit in memory.
introductoryText:
Gives data from sources that name their fields differently one agreed set of field names and types, using rules kept as data: a rules CSV typed into the block, or a rules file. For a fixed mapping set up once, the core **Define schema** block does this in its own settings; this block is for rules you keep in a table and change without editing the workflow. The block works through the data in chunks (it streams), so it suits very large inputs.

**How it works**: each rule names a canonical field and the other names (aliases) it may arrive under. Every input field whose name matches the canonical name or an alias becomes that canonical field. If several input fields match, they are combined: each record takes the first value present, in the order the aliases are listed. The value is then converted to the rule's type; values that can't be converted become empty, and the block's message counts them. Empty values get the rule's default, if it has one.

**How to set it up**: write the rules in **Schema rules**, one rule per line or rules separated by semicolons, as CSV: `canonical, aliases, type, default, format`. A heading row is optional. Or leave it empty and choose a CSV file with the same columns in **Schema rules file**; rules written in the block take precedence. The columns:

- `canonical`: the field name to output.
- `aliases`: other names for it, separated by `|` (or by commas, in a quoted cell).
- `type` (optional): `string` (the default), `number`, `integer`, `date`, `datetime` or `boolean`.
- `default` (optional): the value for empty and unreadable values. Write dates as `2025-01-31`.
- `format` (optional): for dates written as text, the format, such as `%d/%m/%Y` for 31/01/2025. Without it, text dates are read as ISO dates (2025-01-31) or month first; ISO dates are always read.

```
order_id, OrderID|Order No; order_date, Order Date|OrderDate, date, , %d/%m/%Y; quantity, Qty|Quantity|Units, integer; paid, Paid|Is Paid, boolean, false
```

By default each canonical field takes the place of the first input field it came from, and canonical fields with no matching input field are left out. Tick **Output every canonical field** for a fixed schema: all canonical fields, in the rules' order, then any unmapped fields.

options.name: rulesText
options.title: Schema rules
options.description: Rules written in the block as CSV, one rule per line or rules separated by semicolons: canonical, aliases, type, default, format (heading row optional). Takes precedence over the file.

options.name: rules
options.title: Schema rules file
options.description: A CSV file of rules (columns canonical, aliases and, optionally, type, default and format). Used when Schema rules is empty.

options.name: passthrough_unmapped
options.title: Keep unmapped fields
options.description: Pass input fields that match no rule through unchanged. Untick to output the canonical fields only.

options.name: prefer_non_empty_strings
options.title: Treat blank text as missing
options.description: When combining aliases, skip text that is empty or only spaces and take the next alias's value; blank text also gets the default.

options.name: auto_normalise_aliases
options.title: Match names loosely
options.description: Ignore case, and treat spaces, hyphens and underscores alike when matching field names to aliases (Order Date, order_date and ORDER-DATE match). Untick to match names exactly.

options.name: add_missing_canonical
options.title: Output every canonical field
options.description: Output all canonical fields, in the rules' order, even when no input field matches one (it is filled with its default, or left empty). Unmapped fields follow. Unticked, only matched canonical fields are output, in the input's order.

blockOutputs.label: Canonical
blockOutputs.tooltip: The input with its fields renamed, combined and converted as the rules say.
